title: GameSpot’s Exclusive Magic: The Gathering – The Hobbit Cards Turn Death Into An Opportunity
description: Among the flurry of announcements presented at MagicCon Amsterdam was the debut of The Hobbit, Magic: The Gathering’s next expansion and a return to the universe of J.R.R. Tolkien. That debut was only the beginning, though, as we are now in preview season as the set’s release approaches in August. We can exclusively reveal two new Rare cards from the main Hobbit set. One is a powerful green enchantment that can keep your battlefield stocked, and the other is a creature that will slot neatly into mill strategies in multiple formats. First, here’s Part In Friendship. Template_GroupedStyles Part In Friendship (Enchantment) Costs four generic and one green mana Whenever a nontoken creature you control dies, reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card. If its mana value is less than or equal to the number of lands you control, put it onto the battlefield. Otherwise, put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. This ability triggers only once each turn. The solemn scene of Bilbo visiting with Thorin on his deathbed becomes a potent enchantment that will either replenish a fallen creature immediately, or place one into your hand for a future turn. In long, grindy games, it can be a big difference maker, especially if you can manipulate the top of your deck and sacrifice a smaller creature to bring down something massive. Imagine turning a 1/1 token into Craterhoof Behemoth, now that’s friendship. Our second card is The Master of Lake-town. Template_GroupedStyles The Master of Lake-town (Legendary Creature - Human Advisor) Costs one generic and two black mana to cast 3 power/2 toughness Deathtouch Whenever a player loses life, that player mills that many cards. (Damage counts as loss of life.) When The Master of Lake-town dies, draw a card for each graveyard with seven or more cards in it. The greedy and cowardly Master of Lake-town is an interesting addition to mill decks, as he rewards aggression and damage with milling your opponent. Then, should he die in battle, he can immediately draw you a card thanks to the graveyards he helped stock. Self-mill decks won’t get too much out of him, but if your gameplan involves depleting your opponent’s library, you should definitely check this out. The Hobbit expansion for Magic: The Gathering launches August 14 in local game stores and big box retailers. Prerelease events will take place in local game stores starting one week prior, on August 7.

title: The Next Game Of Thrones Game Has Been Delayed

The PC game was originally set for release in 2026, but developer Playside has announced that it's been delayed to "early 2027." "We remain unwavering in our mission to deliver a real-time strategy game set in the world of Westeros that meets the expectations of both RTS players and Game of Thrones fans," the developer said in a blog post. "This decision gives us the time needed to continue building towards that goal and ensure that the game reaches the high level of quality we are aiming for." "Thank you for your patience and continued support. We know the wait has been long, and we do not take your support for granted." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uI9MDe0evFU Announced in 2025, War for Westeros has players controlling one of the franchise's legendary Houses (Stark, Targaryen, or Lannister), or the Night King, with the aim of conquering the Seven Kingdoms. The game has a single-player campaign and multiplayer. The developer has said the aim with War for Westeros is to make you feel like you're playing the TV show. The Game of Thrones series is owned and controlled by Warner Bros. Discovery, which is in the process of being acquired by Paramount for more than $100 billion. title: Hot Toys’ New Marvel Rivals Figure Is Going To Make A Certain Kind Of Collector Very Happy
description: With San Diego Comic-Con kicking off this weekend, Hot Toys has unveiled several new sixth-scale figures, including a Luna Snow collectible that's going to make Marvel Rivals fans very happy. This is the first sixth-scale Marvel Rivals figure from the company, and like all of its other collectibles in this line, it's an impressive-looking replica of the South Korean K-Pop idol turned cryokinetic superhero. When it comes to figures that show plenty of skin, Hot Toys usually uses a specialized silicone body to make them look as life-like as possible. The Luna Snow figure follows this approach, and she's dressed in her default Marvel Rivals costume that features a blue, black, and white color scheme. For the headsculpt, Hot Toys has gone with a sculpted black-and-white two-toned asymmetrical mid-length bob hairstyle, and the head also has separate rolling eyeballs for when you need a subtle expression. As usual, you're getting several swap-out hands, including pairs that allow her to use her iconic "hand heart" and "finger heart" gesture emotes. Her jacket also looks like a work of mini-tailoring art with its straps, buckles, and studs, and other accessories include a floating music notes effect, a stand featuring the Marvel Rivals logo and character nameplate, and an attack effect. There's no release date or pricing yet, but Hot Toys usually announces these figures with a minimum of a year's lead time and a retail price of around $300 through vendors like Sideshow Collectibles. If a superhero K-pop star doesn't appeal to you, you can also check out the new--and very limited--edition of Sam Porter Bridges from Death Stranding 2: On the Beach that Hot Toys revealed. While the company revealed figures based on the intrepid courier and his nemesis, Higgs, last year, this new limited-edition version features a Timefall-resistant suit that's adorned with illustrations by Junji Ito, one of the greatest horror manga storytellers of the modern era. Other figures coming from Hot Toys include a monstrous Alien Queen from Aliens, an intimidating Savage Hulk from Spider-Man: Brand New Day, a quarter-scale replica of The Dark Knight's Joker, and a whole lot of Kamen Riders. Last week also saw the first look at a new Street Fighter 2 Cammy figure from Infinity Studio, a massive 1:3 scale replica of the M. Bison clone. Meanwhile, Marvel Rivals has gotten a substantial update for Season 9. A ground-up rework has introduced new strategies to the game, the Team-Up System has been transformed, and the X-Man Jubilee has been added to the game roster. title: Call Of Duty Movie Gets A Key Update About Its Setting
description: Activision has clarified a key detail about the upcoming Call of Duty movie from director Peter Berg and writer Taylor Sheridan. At Fanatics Fest this weekend, Berg confirmed that the movie takes place in the Modern Warfare universe. This is a major detail, considering the Call of Duty series is known for its multiple brands, including Modern Warfare, Black Ops, and others, each with its own distinct tones, settings, and characters. Many were wondering which universe the film might take place in, and now we know. The Call of Duty movie releases in theaters on June 30, 2028. There is no word yet on the cast or specific plot points, however. https://twitter.com/CallofDuty/status/2078547067577004220 The Call of Duty movie is in the works at Paramount, which is owned by billionaire David Ellison, who himself is a big fan of Call of Duty. Paramount is in the midst of trying to buy Warner Bros. Discovery for more than $100 billion. Director Peter Berg is known for his action and war movies, including Lone Survivor and Deepwater Horizon. In the world of TV, he garnered praise for the drama miniseries Painkiller, which was about the opioid epidemic in America. As for writer Taylor Sheridan, he's known for writing and directing the movies Sicario, Wind River, and Hell or High Water. He also created the popular Yellowstone TV series. In recent times, he's railed against Hollywood media, saying he gets excited by rage-baiting the press with his works. Just because a movie has been announced, that doesn't necessarily mean it'll ever be made, however. There are dozens of video game movies currently at some stage of production, and no one expects them all to come out. This is just the latest attempt to make a Call of Duty movie. Activision first announced plans for an entire connected universe of Call of Duty movies more than 10 years ago, and nothing ever came of that. As for the Modern Warfare game series, the newest entry, Modern Warfare 4, comes out this October. The game will have a free open beta at some point before launch, and preordering gets you in early.

title: Xbox Explains What Makes A Game An Xbox Exclusive
description: Amidst mass layoffs and increasing hardware prices, one of the other side effects of the Xbox "reset" is a renewed focus on console exclusives. While we know that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution will only be available on Xbox Series X|S and PC, they won't be the only two exclusives landing on those platforms. "I can assure you, Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are not the only titles we're planning," chief strategy officer Matthew Ball said to GamesRadar. "To grow a platform like ours, you have to have exclusive games and services. These are not going to be the only two titles. To return our platform to consistent growth, we need a reliable pipeline of exclusive games. Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are just the first." While Xbox has its eye on drawing more people to its platforms through the power of exclusives--it is aiming to "entertain" a billion people every day, eventually--not every game will be locked to Xbox. Ball added that "large live-service titles" will continue to be multiplatform titles, and some single-player games could also make their way to hardware like the PS5. As Ball explained, Microsoft has a "framework" in place for deciding which games will be Xbox exclusives and which ones will expand to additional platforms, as the company decides on a case-by-case basis. "I recognize that this approach is not obvious to all of our players, and we are committed to making this clearer," Ball said. While the new Gears of War and Clockwork Revolution won't be landing on PS5, Halo: Campaign Evolved and Fable will be available on the Sony platform the same day and date as the Xbox and PC versions of the game. Halo: Campaign Evolved executive producer Damon Conn added that going multiplatform was the right approach for the game as it celebrates its 25th anniversary, as this will allow friends to enjoy shared experiences no matter which system they're on. While Xbox seems adamant to offer exclusive games once again, one analyst believes that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are being used as sacrificial lambs to win back hearts and minds, following several months of bad news at the Microsoft gaming division. title: Most Nintendo Employees Found Out About Tears Of The Kingdom When You Did
description: Nintendo has a good track record when it comes to keeping secrets, and in the case of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, the Breath of the Wild sequel's announcement was one of the company's most confidential projects. In fact, the game's existence was so secret that many Nintendo employees only found out about it when it was teased during the E3 2019 Nintendo Direct livestream. According to former Nintendo of America marketing and PR leads Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang, Tears of the Kingdom had a "higher level" of security than any other Nintendo project that they worked on, and they claimed that only a small handful of people at NoA knew about it. https://youtu.be/eeyniV4efYM?t=3329 Ellis, who was the director of social media marketing and original content at the time, said that he was trusted enough to be told about the sequel and that he had to work on it in secret, with his social team none the wiser. "I had a ton to do. There was this big communications team, like an E3 machine, cranking out materials, and obviously the main place for this was in the Nintendo Direct," Ellis said. It became clear, I have to do these different teams' jobs in secret, and when this happens, feed them this thing and tell them what to do with it." Yang added that the official teaser was a big hit amongst the surprised Nintendo employees, with staff promptly celebrating the surprise reveal. A few years later, Tears of the Kingdom landed on Switch consoles and earned rave reviews across the world for how it expanded on Breath of the Wild and pushed its gameplay systems to new heights. Both games were also updated for the Switch 2 when it launched last year. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3DRARZQexW4 The franchise has had a constant presence on Nintendo hardware for several years now, with last year's Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment acting as a prequel to Tears of the Kingdom by detailing the events of Zelda's trip back in time. This year will see the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and in the not-so-distant future, we're also getting a live-action Zelda movie and some new action figures.

title: Marathon Game Director Leaves Bungie At A Tumultuous Time
description: Marathon game director Joe Ziegler has announced that he's leaving Bungie for a new job, and his departure comes at a tumultuous time for the studio. Ziegler said in a note that taking over for him as game director on Marathon will be Del Chafe III, who was previously the assistant game director. Chafe III will work alongside creative director Julia Nardin to "guide the game forward." "Both of them have been operating in a strong leadership capacity for the team and are ready to guide Marathon into the next chapter with an even better and brighter future," Ziegler said. "I'm proud of them and I'm excited to see them helm the future of this crazy little world we've created together." Marathon has lost another game director.Ziegler said he is "heading to something new, somewhere else," and will announce his new job soon. "I just want to say a deeply heartfelt thank you to all of you for supporting me and Marathon in our windy mission to bring a dark and terrifying space survival frontier to your screen," Ziegler said. "The mission will continue in new and surprising ways so stay tuned for what this team has in store for you!" Ziegler was not Marathon's first game director. Christopher Barrett was game director on the project until he was dismissed over misconduct allegations. Earlier this month, Barrett settled his case with Bungie and Sony. Ziegler joined Bungie at the end of 2022, following a 12-year run at Riot Games. He's leaving Bungie at a challenging time for the Sony-owned studio, which enacted a round of layoffs at the end of June. The cuts impacted the Destiny and Marathon teams.

title: Zero Parades Dev Announces Layoffs Despite Game’s Critical Acclaim
description: Another day, another layoff announcement. This time it comes from Zero Parades: For Dead Spies developer ZA/UM, which said on social media that despite the game's critical acclaim, the studio can't sustain the size of its team. ZA/UM took to Bluesky on July 17 to share the unfortunate news. The team said that although Zero Parades reviewed well, "its commercial performance" made it difficult for the studio to maintain its current employee count. As a result, the company has "served redundancy or at-risk notices" to up to 32 staffers at the RPG studio. https://bsky.app/profile/zaumstudio.bsky.social/post/3mqu7qi4txc24 "Throughout this difficult process, we have continued to consult and work with representatives of the ZA/UM Workers' Alliance," the studio wrote on Bluesky. "This changes the shape of ZA/UM, but not its purpose. Our artistic standards remain unchanged: We will persist." Zero Parades: For Dead Spies is the second game from ZA/UM following the studio's 2019 outing Disco Elysium. Released in May 2026 for PC with a PS5 version coming later this year, Zero Parades is an isometric espionage RPG about a female operative named Hershel Wilk who's tasked with uncovering the secrets of her haunted past. It's chilling and thrilling in the best ways, receiving an 8/10 in GameSpot's Zero Parades: For Dead Spies review and an 83 score on Metacritic. ZA/UM is the latest developer to suffer layoffs, as 2026 has seen the games industry rattled by myriad studio closures and employee terminations. Earlier this month, Xbox let go of 1,600 staffers as part of its big "reset" earlier this month, with another 1,600 planned to get laid off in the next 12 months. Skate studio Full Circle was also hit with layoffs in February 2026, as was 2XKO developer Riot Games in the same month. Meanwhile, Sony shut down Bluepoint Games, the developer responsible for some excellent remakes, in February as well. It seems like everywhere you look, another layoff happens.
